NEW YMCA ADMINSTRATOR 


PROMISES ACTION, NOT DREAMS 

Ways in which dreams of social improvement can be given 
substance are getting top-priority attention from all YMCAs 
in Greater Montreal. 

"Lofty idealism alone won't solve contemporary human 
problems", notes R.G. Rogers, 37, in his first official 
statement as General Secretary of the Montreal YMCA. 

"Paths to solutions become even more clouded when there 
igs ambiguity of purpose”, he warns. 

Mr. Rogers and Assistant General Secretary, R.D. Bannerman, 
41, were appointed to their new posts July 1, 1968. 

" Our emphasis is,increasingly, on the development of 
operating objectives which can convert general aspirations 
into specific and positive actions", says Mr. Rogers. "At 
the same time, we are increasing the relevancy of our 
activities to current individual and social needs." 

He stresses that while the YMCA of Greater Montreal is 
one association, centralizing its information and planning, 
"the action is decentralized through eight branches and camps." 

"Working within the broad policy set by the Metropolitan 
Board, each of these operating units sets its own priorities 
and develops the types of programs and activities most needed 
in the communities they serve."
